adjudication_records.issue_text: PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey uses a try/catch around findElement + assertThat(element, nullValue()) construct that swallows exceptions, making the webauthn-button-absence assertion a no-op that cannot distinguish element-missing from other exceptions; should use driver.findElements(...).isEmpty()

adjudication.rationale: In `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey`, the absence check is implemented as `try { driver.findElement(...); assertThat(..., nullValue()); fail(...); } catch (Exception ...) { /* expected */ }`. This does correctly fail if the element exists (because `assertThat(WebElement, nullValue())` will throw an `AssertionError`, which is not caught), but it also treats *any* `Exception` (e.g., unexpected WebDriver errors) as “expected”, which can mask real failures and make the assertion less reliable. Using `findElements(...).isEmpty()` would avoid exception-driven control flow and not swallow unrelated exceptions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UsernamePasswordForm.java:135-137 error path during re-auth for a user with zero passkeys: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user) is true for any re-auth user in a passkeys-enabled realm, causing fillContextForm to fall into the unidentified-user/conditional-UI branch on a form with USERNAME_HIDDEN, and the edge case has no effective test coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes `UsernamePasswordForm` call `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` whenever `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` is true (i.e., `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`), regardless of whether the user actually has any WebAuthn credentials. That part of the finding is verifiable. Also, `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` overrides `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators()` to always return false, which bypasses the shown “user identified / has authenticators” check path in `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm(...)` and could plausibly lead to UI being prepared even when a re-auth user has zero passkeys. However, the diff snippet doesn’t include the remainder of `fillContextForm`, so it’s not fully provable this becomes broken behavior; it is a concrete edge-case/coverage concern and there’s no test specifically for “realm passkeys enabled + re-auth user has zero passkeys.”

adjudication_records.issue_text: AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError can force USERNAME_HIDDEN on a conditional-UI error form where the user is not yet identified, hiding the username input and making the page unusable; the relevant test never asserts username field visibility

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError only hides the username when the auth-session note USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH parses to true. That note is explicitly documented (in AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator) as indicating the user was already set in the auth context before the authenticator ran, i.e., the user is identified. The finding’s scenario (“conditional-UI error form where the user is not yet identified” but username forced hidden) is not supported by the shown code changes, because there’s no path in the diff that sets this note when the user is null/unidentified. The comment about tests not asserting username visibility is also not a specific, diff-provable problem with correctness; the diff’s tests focus on presence of the WebAuthn form and re-auth flows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UsernameForm.java:47 — Linked-broker re-authentication path silently bypassed when passkeys enabled; IDP-only users lose IDP re-auth option, and broker path is untested

adjudication.rationale: In UsernameForm.authenticate the diff changes the early-return optimization from `if (context.getUser() != null)` to `if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled())`. This does not “silently bypass” the linked-broker re-authentication path; it does the opposite: when passkeys are enabled it avoids skipping the form, so execution continues (and any linked-broker handling that occurs when the form is shown would still be reachable). The claim that “IDP-only users lose IDP re-auth option” is not verifiable from this diff, and the diff does not show removal of broker/IDP UI logic. While it’s true no new tests explicitly cover linked-broker re-auth with passkeys, the finding asserts broken behavior that the shown change doesn’t substantiate.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UsernamePasswordForm.java:160 — isConditionalPasskeysEnabled never checks user actually has a WebAuthn credential, so password-only users see a passkey option that cannot succeed

adjudication.rationale: In UsernamePasswordForm, isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) only checks that passkeys are enabled, webauthnAuth is non-null, and user != null; it does not check whether the identified user has any WebAuthn/passwordless credentials before calling webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) (in both authenticate() and challenge()). The diff does not show whether fillContextForm internally suppresses the passkey UI when no authenticators exist, so the claimed end-user-visible failure (“password-only users see a passkey option that cannot succeed”) is not directly verifiable from the provided hunks, but the missing eligibility check is a concrete, diff-grounded edge-case/UX concern introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UsernameForm.java:47 — Realm-wide passkeys check forces username page onto passkey-less users during re-auth; correct gate is per-user credential, not realm policy

adjudication.rationale: In `UsernameForm.authenticate`, the previous re-auth shortcut (`if (context.getUser() != null) context.success()`) is now disabled whenever `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` is true. From the diff, the only gating pattern added elsewhere (`UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel)`) checks `webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()` (realm policy/feature) and `user != null`, but does not check whether the specific user actually has any WebAuthn/passkey credentials. That supports the finding that the new gate is not per-user-credential-based and could cause the username page to be shown during re-auth even for users without passkeys when passkeys are enabled realm-wide. However, this is primarily a UX/flow optimization concern (extra form step) rather than a clearly broken correctness/security defect proven by the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.java:197-201 — Scope drift: conditional-UI webauthn form now shown during normal first-time login, changing regular login rendering beyond re-auth intent

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change normal (non re-auth) login rendering: in PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest the expectation is updated to require the WebAuthn conditional-UI form to be present on the username+password page after the username is selected (lines ~197-201 in the test). This aligns with UsernamePasswordForm now calling `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` whenever `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` (i.e., passkeys enabled and `user != null`), which will also be true during a standard username-first login flow once the user is identified—not only during re-authentication. Whether that’s “scope drift” vs intended is subjective, but the diff-grounded concern (broader UI behavior change) is real and specific, not a verifiable defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.java:58 — USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH visibility widened from protected to public, unnecessarily expanding public SPI surface instead of relocating the constant

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` in `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator` from `protected static final` to `public static final`. This is used by `AuthenticatorUtils` via a `static import` (`import static ...AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH;`), which would not compile with `protected` visibility across packages. While not a functional defect, it does widen the publicly accessible API surface of a browser authenticator class to support reuse from a util package; a reviewer could reasonably question whether the constant should instead live in a shared utility/constant location to avoid expanding public surface.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inverted user-null condition in UsernamePasswordForm.java:113-116 & 136-138 causes conditional passkeys form data to be dropped from initial-login error pages, since isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) requires user != null but context user remains null after a bad password during initial login, funneling users to password-only retry

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `UsernamePasswordForm.challenge(context, error, field)` changes the condition from `context.getUser() == null && ...isPasskeysEnabled()` to `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, and `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` explicitly requires `user != null`. This is a verifiable inversion: previously the webauthn/passkeys context (`webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)`) would be set up specifically when the user was null (a common state on initial login error retries if the flow clears the user), but after this change it will not run when `context.getUser()` is null, so the passkeys-related form attributes/data can be missing on those error pages.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing test coverage for the user==null error re-challenge path in UsernamePasswordForm, the case whose behavior flipped (tests only cover re-auth with user already set)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the error re-challenge behavior in `UsernamePasswordForm.challenge(context, error, field)` from only filling WebAuthn context when `context.getUser() == null` (old code) to filling it only when `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, which explicitly requires `user != null` (new `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`). That is a flipped branch for the `user == null` error path. The added/modified tests in this diff focus on re-authentication scenarios where the user is already identified (e.g., `prompt=login`) and on keeping WebAuthn UI available during re-auth; they do not exercise the `user == null` error re-challenge path whose behavior changed. This is a specific, diff-grounded gap in test coverage rather than a directly provable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UsernameForm.java:47 realm-level passkeys flag forces a username form on re-auth for users with no passkey, conflating 'passkeys available in realm' with 'passkeys usable by this user' and adding unnecessary friction; should use a per-user credential check

adjudication.rationale: In UsernameForm.authenticate the skip-on-reauth path changed from `if (context.getUser() != null) { ... context.success(); }` to `if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()) { ... }` (services/.../UsernameForm.java). This means when conditional passkeys are enabled, re-authentication will no longer bypass the username form even though the user is already identified, which can add extra UI friction. The diff does not show any per-user credential check here (it gates purely on `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()`), so the concern about conflating a global/passkeys-enabled condition with whether passkeys are actually usable for the current user is a reasonable review issue, though it’s more UX/flow design than a concrete correctness defect proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The decision of whether the webauthn form renders is split across two classes under misleading names (isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user) and shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators()), duplicating the intent in three places; should be a single named predicate like shouldRenderPasskeysUi(context) on the shared base class

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces/uses multiple predicates that collectively govern whether passkeys/WebAuthn UI elements are populated/shown, but the decision is spread across classes and methods with overlapping intent: `UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel)` gates `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` in both `authenticate()` and `challenge()`, while `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm()` now gates showing authenticators via `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context)` (default `context.getUser()!=null`) and `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` overrides it to always false. Additionally `UsernameForm.authenticate()` adds `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` (method not shown here) as another gating point. This is a real maintainability/architecture issue created/exposed by the change (duplicated and split rendering conditions), but not a verifiable correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() guard applies to all paths where a user is already set in the auth context, not just re-authentication, forcing Kerberos/SPNEGO, identity-broker link, and organization selection users through a username form in passkeys-enabled realms even if they hold no passkey credential

adjudication.rationale: In `UsernameForm.authenticate`, the early-success shortcut was changed from `if (context.getUser() != null) { ... context.success(); }` to `if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()) { ... }`. This means whenever a user is pre-set in the `AuthenticationFlowContext` and conditional passkeys are enabled, the authenticator will no longer skip the username form, regardless of *why* the user was set (not limited to the re-authentication case described in the comment). The diff does not show any additional narrowing (e.g., checking re-authentication notes or whether the user actually has passkey credentials), so the concern about broadened impact is diff-grounded, though the specific affected mechanisms (Kerberos/SPNEGO, broker link, org selection) are not directly evidenced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing test coverage for the Kerberos/broker path affected by the new passkeys conditional guard

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new conditional guard in `UsernameForm.authenticate()` (`if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled())`) that changes behavior specifically when a user is already set in the flow context (a situation that can occur in re-authentication / pre-identified-user scenarios, e.g., broker/kerberos style flows) and passkeys are enabled. The added/updated tests focus on passkeys re-authentication (`prompt=login`) and WebAuthn UI presence, but there is no diff-visible test exercising the “user already set” path together with linked broker handling (`hasLinkedBrokers(context)`) under the new guard. So the concern about missing test coverage for that affected path is specific and diff-grounded, even though the exact Kerberos/broker mechanism isn’t shown in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test at PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.java:197-203 silently inverts a previously-asserted accepted behavior from NoSuchElementException for the webauth form to notNullValue, rewriting the test to match the code rather than an agreed spec

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest to expect the WebAuthn form to be present (notNullValue) where it previously expected absence via NoSuchElementException. However, the diff also changes production code to deliberately keep/enable conditional passkeys UI when a user is already identified (e.g., UsernamePasswordForm now calls webauthnAuth.fillContextForm when isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) is true, and new tests are added for re-authentication with passkeys). The claim that this inverts an “agreed spec” or is “rewriting the test to match the code rather than spec” cannot be verified from the diff alone, since no spec/contract is shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() in WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator unconditionally returns false, so when the conditional-UI WebAuthn step runs as an actual 2FA authentication step the registered authenticator list is never rendered, including in createErrorResponse where the user has no visible fallback list

adjudication.rationale: The diff does make `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators()` always return false, which prevents `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm()` from rendering the `WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean` list. However, the change is explicitly intentional per the added comment: "Do not show authenticators during login with conditional passkeys (For example during username/password)". The finding’s claim that this class is used as an "actual 2FA authentication step" and therefore breaks 2FA/fallback rendering is not verifiable from the diff; the normal 2FA behavior would be handled by `WebAuthnAuthenticator`, which still shows authenticators when `context.getUser() != null` via its default `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UsernameForm.authenticate calls no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() which is not defined in the diff on a common parent, and the no-arg variant skips the webauthnAuth != null guard, risking NPE and behavioral divergence from UsernamePasswordForm's predicate on when re-auth username prompt is bypassed

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `UsernameForm.authenticate` now calls a no-arg `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()`, but the diff does not show the full `UsernameForm` class or its supertypes, so it’s not verifiable from the diff whether this method is undefined (compile error) or whether it lacks a `webauthnAuth != null` guard. The alleged NPE risk and behavioral divergence depend on the unseen implementation of `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` in `UsernameForm`/parents, which cannot be confirmed from the provided hunks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In UsernamePasswordForm.java:158, requiring user != null in isConditionalPasskeysEnabled means webauthn form data is no longer populated during anonymous first-time login, breaking passkey login for non-conditional-UI setups using the plain WebAuthnAuthenticator, with no test coverage for this regression

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a concrete behavior change: in UsernamePasswordForm, webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) is now gated by isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), and isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) returns true only when user != null. Previously, challenge(...) explicitly populated WebAuthn context when context.getUser() == null and passkeys were enabled, so anonymous/first-step pages could get WebAuthn form data. Whether this actually breaks passkey login cannot be verified from the diff alone (it depends on how templates/use of fillContextForm works), and the finding’s claim about “plain WebAuthnAuthenticator non-conditional-UI setups” isn’t substantiated by the shown changes. Still, the change introduces a plausible untested edge-case (anonymous login page with passkeys enabled) that is diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Swallow-catch idiom in PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest (reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey) makes the test pass on unrelated WebDriver failures like StaleElementReferenceException or TimeoutException, and the fail() line is dead code; should use assertThrows instead

adjudication.rationale: In `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey`, the diff adds `try { driver.findElement(...); ... } catch (Exception nsee) { // expected }` to assert the WebAuthn form is absent. `findElement` signals absence via `NoSuchElementException`, but this code catches *any* `Exception`, so unrelated WebDriver failures (e.g., timeouts, stale element, driver errors) would also be treated as “expected” and let the test continue. Also, `MatcherAssert.assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue())` is not a meaningful assertion because `findElement` does not return null on absence; it throws, so the subsequent `fail("Not expected...")` is effectively unreachable for the common “element present” case (the assertion would throw `AssertionError` first). Using `assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` (as already used elsewhere in the diff) would avoid swallowing unrelated failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Refactored re-auth error attributes (USERNAME_HIDDEN, REGISTRATION_DISABLED) set by AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError have zero assertions anywhere in the diff, so a regression dropping the call would pass the suite

adjudication.rationale: The diff moves the re-authentication form setup logic (setting LoginFormsProvider.USERNAME_HIDDEN and REGISTRATION_DISABLED) into AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError and replaces the prior inline block in AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler() with that call. The added/modified tests assert things like presence of the WebAuthn form, attempted username, and info/error messages, but none assert that the username field is hidden or that registration is disabled during re-auth flows. So if a future change accidentally removed/omitted the setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(...) call, the tests shown here would still likely pass, leaving this refactor-specific behavior unprotected.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError call in WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse conditional-UI error path is untested — no test triggers a passkey failure during re-authentication

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new call to `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context);` inside `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse(...)`, i.e., specifically on the conditional-passkeys error path (“the passkey failed, show error...”). The newly added/updated tests cover re-authentication success with passkeys (e.g., `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication`, `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication`) and password failure during re-authentication followed by passkey/password success (`webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey`), but none clearly trigger a *passkey failure* during re-authentication that would exercise `createErrorResponse(...)` and thus the new setup call. This is a concrete missing-test concern for newly added nontrivial error-handling logic, not a functional defect proven by the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate: conditional passkeys UI no longer initialized for unidentified users — isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) requires user != null, so first-visit login pages lose WebAuthn setup, breaking conditional-mediation passkey autofill for passkey-only users (P1)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes UsernamePasswordForm to only call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) when isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) is true, and isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) explicitly requires user != null. Previously, authenticate() initialized WebAuthn context whenever passkeys were enabled (no user-null check), and challenge(error, field) initialized WebAuthn context specifically when context.getUser() == null. This is a behavior flip: unidentified/first-visit pages (context.getUser()==null) will no longer get WebAuthn form/context setup from UsernamePasswordForm, which can disable conditional passkeys UI/autofill in that scenario.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UsernameForm.java:47: 'if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled())' silently skips linked-broker re-authentication handling when conditional passkeys are enabled, leaving broker-credential users unable to complete re-authentication (P2)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `UsernameForm.authenticate()` to only auto-succeed (skip the username form) when `context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()`. The linked-broker handling (`if (!this.hasLinkedBrokers(context)) { context.success(); }`) was only used to decide whether to skip the form; users *with* linked brokers were already not auto-skipped and would continue through the normal form flow. With conditional passkeys enabled, the code now always continues through the form even when `context.getUser() != null`, which does not, based on the diff, prevent linked-broker users from re-authenticating; it just avoids the optimization of skipping the form. The claim that broker-credential users become unable to complete re-authentication is not supported by the shown changes.
